rv.q: This handsomely mounted revival of Lerner and Loewe's 1960 musical is both faithful to the original and subtly updated for contemporary audiences.
This new 'Camelot' doesn't quite achieve the impossible dream of its legendary predecessor, but it succeeds in making Lerner and Loewe's score feel vital again.
The result is an at times dramatically lagging, but consistently polished and warming tale playing out at Lincoln Center’s Theater.

If this Camelot is a bit confused on whether it wants to be a majestic golden age musical or a gritty take on the shaky foundations of a monarchical ménage à trois, it pulls through on the strength of its cast, which tightly brings the work’s brief shining moment into glorious light.
